findings.summary: runChannelWrite calls decideTermination with postWriteState.cards, which the code itself documents (lines 1283-1292) as excluding clues published during this tick. On a harvest tick the parent card is CAS'd to explored (inFlight becomes 0) while the newly published proposed clues are invisible, so the termination input sees inFlight===0 and proposed===0 and, once zeroGrowthRounds has reached the threshold, reports state==='converged' in the very tick that created new pending work. hasPendingWork was compensated for exactly this omission (cluesPublished > 0) but the termination call immediately below was not, so the delivered terminal state can falsely claim convergence — the completeness-misrepresentation the spec (§0.2/§3.4) exists to prevent. Passing the consistent pre-write board (or a board augmented with this tick's published clues) would not produce this false positive.

The coverage half of the termination input has no production power: coveredClueIds comes from assembleBoard over the board channel read (src/tick-run.ts:1188-1194 reads only opts.channelId and the runs channel), but production publishes research.evidence.v2 to a separate evidence channel (src/harvest.ts:337-341 with EVIDENCE_CHANNEL=research:v1-deep-research.evidence vs TICK_CHANNEL=research:v1-deep-research.index in profiles/deploy/production.env:9-10), which the --run path never reads. Coverage is therefore structurally 0 on every production tick, so 'coverage > prevCoverage' is never true, zeroGrowthRounds increments unconditionally, and the reset branch that R3 asserts is unreachable in production. R2/R3 pass only because the tests plant research.evidence.v2 messages onto the board channel (test/g4b-termination-wiring.test.ts:88-99 and 242-251), a configuration production never has; the result is that 'converged' degenerates into 'the pre-write snapshot momentarily had no in_flight/proposed cards', not 'coverage stopped growing'.

parseTerminationFromBody (and TriggerBodyTerminationError) has zero production callers — the production body parser is a separately written node script embedded in tick.md:60-88. The R5 TypeScript assertions and mutation S2 (which the dev-note says was applied to parseTerminationFromBody) therefore exercise code the production path never runs, and the two parsers can silently diverge; only the single bash-level R5 case actually guards production behaviour.

A continuation body that carries neither counter field is silently treated as first-round 0/0 instead of failing loudly: the parser only special-cases 'both fields absent' and never checks the discriminating 'seed' marker, so a body such as {"tick":true} (a continuation body that lost its counters) silently resets zeroGrowthRounds — precisely the silent-reset failure mode R5 forbids. Keying first-round semantics on the seed marker rather than on 'no counters present' would close this.

The trigger-body parser captures stderr into a fixed-name scratch file 'trigger_body_err.txt' in the tick node's current working directory. If that directory is not writable the redirect fails, the command substitution returns non-zero and the tick exits 1 with an empty 'cat' of a missing file — a loud failure attributed to a bad trigger body when the real cause is the working directory. Use mktemp or capture stderr without touching the CWD.
